claimSummary.en: Pre-excitation may be subtle with an apparently normal PR; variable fusion can obscure delta. One recording cannot establish pathway risk.

claimSummary.es: La pérdida gradual de delta puede representar más conducción por el nodo AV y no prueba bloqueo de la vía; una vía oculta solo retrógrada no produce preexcitación anterógrada en el ECG.
claimSummary.en: Gradual delta loss may represent greater AV-node contribution and does not prove pathway block; a retrograde-only concealed pathway does not cause antegrade ECG pre-excitation.

references.limitations: The review treats unequivocal abrupt loss as reassuring; the 2024 prospective referral cohort limits categorical claims that it excludes dangerous conduction.

references.limitations: Referral cohort and EPS surrogate, not observed sudden-death outcomes. Low-risk exercise included absent delta before exercise or abrupt loss; isoproterenol changes classification. No individual probability derived.

claimSummary.en: An isolated sinus rate <50 bpm or pause >3 s does not establish sinus-node dysfunction. Review subtle symptoms, medications, electrolytes, thyroid function and exercise response as appropriate.

references.limitations: Narrative synthesis. Numeric rate/pause thresholds describe findings, not pacing indications or a detector validation.

claimSummary.es: Mobitz II exige PP estable, PR igual antes y después de una sola P bloqueada y al menos dos P conducidas consecutivas. El enlentecimiento sinusal y extrasístoles ocultas pueden simularlo; 2:1 no se subtipifica.
claimSummary.en: Mobitz II requires stable PP, equal PR before and after a single blocked P, and at least two consecutive conducted P waves. Sinus slowing and concealed ectopy can mimic it; 2:1 block cannot be subtyped.

references.limitations: Expert definitions and examples, no validated aggregate-feature classifier. Global P/QRS ratio and PR variability cannot verify these beat-level requirements.
references.population: Adults with apparent second-degree AV block; expert ECG review with illustrative tracings, no prospective diagnostic cohort.

claimSummary.en: Haemodynamic stability does not distinguish VT from SVT; irregularity does not exclude VT. Compare baseline ECG, review medications and metabolic causes; algorithms can misclassify.

references.limitations: Narrative review; referral/EP-derived diagnostic algorithms do not supply individual confidence. No drug choice is generated.
